moat_against: No scale or cost advantage vs Tesla and legacy OEMs — automotive gross profit still negative in Q2 2026 while software/services carried consolidated gross profit
Customer/partner concentration — VW JV roughly 60% of software and services revenue per research; Amazon dominates commercial vans
Capital intensity with no self-funding — negative OCF, ~$1.7B/yr capex, Georgia plant ahead, repeated equity issuance; US EV demand fell after the $7,500 credit expired Sep 2025
No proven pricing power into profitability — losses persist at every volume printed so far
moat_for: Software / electrical architecture validated externally — Volkswagen JV (RV Tech) is a major high-margin software-and-services revenue source and strategic capital partner
Premium adventure brand with demonstrated demand — R2 launch demand, record demo drives in Q2 2026, deliveries growing into a shrinking US EV market
Amazon commercial-van anchor and Uber robotaxi commitment diversify revenue beyond premium consumer SUVs
Direct sales/service model and vertical integration — control of customer experience and the vehicle data/autonomy stack
moat_justification: Real brand and technology differentiation — a loyal premium adventure brand, vertically integrated software/electrical architecture that Volkswagen paid billions to access through the JV, and an Amazon commercial-van anchor — but no durable cost advantage, no network effect, low consumer switching costs, and no proven pricing power or returns on capital: the company has never produced positive owner's earnings at any scale so far, and third-party assessors assign it no moat. Scale is the core gap — guided 65,000-70,000 deliveries in 2026 against incumbents at millions of units.
name: Rivian Automotive, Inc.
one_liner: Weak-moat EV maker, moat 4/10, R2 ramp and VW software JV are real — but owner's earnings are negative in all 5 filed years (median -$3.50/sh, TTM -$3.33/sh) with operating cash flow itself negative, so it cannot clear 15% at $13.02; Tier F until OCF turns positive enough to cover capex + SBC.
